summary: Most nationalities can obtain an Iranian tourist visa online or on arrival at major airports, and a growing list of countries enters visa-free, but US, UK and Canadian citizens must book a guided tour and obtain an embassy visa with prior authorization, and Israeli passport holders are not admitted at all.

fee.notes: Indicative. Fees vary widely by nationality and are usually paid when the visa is collected at a consulate or on arrival with the eVisa approval code.
Approximate. The fee varies by nationality and is payable in cash (euros) at the airport; compliant travel insurance is checked and can be bought on the spot.

visaTypes.name: Embassy Visa with authorized guide (US, UK, Canada)

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months on arrival and must contain no evidence of travel to Israel.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required only if you arrive from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission.

travelInsurance.text: Medical travel insurance valid for Iran is required and is checked for visas on arrival. Many Western policies exclude Iran because of sanctions. Read the small print; a compliant local policy can be bought at the airport on arrival.

onwardTicket.text: Visa-on-arrival applicants must show a return or onward ticket and accommodation details for at least the first nights.

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is published, but bring all the cash you will need, as foreign bank cards do not work in Iran.

currencyLimits.text: Foreign currency worth EUR 10,000 or more (or equivalent) must be declared on arrival.

notes: Alcohol is illegal in Iran and may not be imported under any circumstances.
Drones and satellite communication devices are confiscated and can lead to arrest. Leave them at home.
Any evidence of travel to Israel in your passport will lead to refusal of entry.

payments.text: Foreign bank cards do not work in Iran because of sanctions. Bring everything you need in cash (euros or US dollars) and exchange gradually, or load a prepaid local tourist card. Prices are often quoted in tomans: 1 toman = 10 rials.

safety.text: Several Western governments advise against all travel to Iran, citing the risk of arbitrary detention — particularly for dual nationals and journalists — alongside regional conflict. Ordinary crime is low and visitors are generally received warmly, but the political risk is real: check your government's advisory before deciding to go.

bestTimeToVisit.text: Spring (March–May) and fall (September–November) are ideal for Tehran, Isfahan, Shiraz and Yazd; summers are fiercely hot in the center and south.

idp.text: Iran is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

source.name: UN Treaty Collection — Convention on Road Traffic (Vienna, 1968), status of parties
source.instrument: Convention on Road Traffic, Vienna, 8 November 1968 (UNTS vol. 1042, p. 17)

driving.text: Iran is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Iran yet.

tips.text: Women, including foreign visitors, are legally required to cover their hair with a headscarf in public and to wear loose clothing covering arms and legs; men should avoid shorts. Enforcement varies, but the law applies from the moment you board an Iran-bound flight.

US, UK and Canadian citizens must travel on a pre-approved itinerary with a government-licensed guide, are fingerprinted on arrival, and typically wait a month or more for the visa authorization code. Book through a specialist operator well ahead.
Visa on arrival is issued only at major international airports (Tehran IKA, Shiraz, Isfahan, Mashhad and others) — never at land borders. Arriving overland, you need the eVisa approval first.

Iran does not recognize dual nationality — dual citizens, especially Iranian dual nationals, have been detained and cannot receive consular help. Many governments explicitly advise dual nationals not to travel.
Budget your whole trip in cash before arrival — euros are easiest to exchange — and change money at licensed exchange offices (sarrafi), which give far better rates than banks.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Iran?
faq.answer: Most nationalities do, but it is straightforward: apply online at evisa.mfa.ir or, if arriving by air, obtain a 30-day visa on arrival at major airports. A growing list of countries — including Turkey, several Gulf and Asian states and much of the former Soviet space — enters visa-free. US, UK and Canadian citizens are the exception and need an embassy visa with a guided tour.

faq.question: Can Americans visit Iran?
faq.answer: Yes, but only on an organized, pre-approved itinerary with a licensed guide. The visa requires a Ministry of Foreign Affairs authorization code arranged through a tour operator, takes a month or more, and applicants are fingerprinted on arrival. The same rules apply to UK and Canadian citizens. Note that the US government advises against all travel to Iran.

faq.question: Can I visit Iran if I have been to Israel?
faq.answer: Evidence of travel to Israel — stamps, visas, or border-crossing stamps from Egyptian or Jordanian land borders with Israel — leads to refusal of an Iranian visa or entry. Israeli citizens are barred entirely.

faq.question: Can I use my credit card in Iran?
faq.answer: No. International card networks do not operate in Iran because of sanctions. Bring your entire budget in cash (euros or dollars are best) or arrange a prepaid Iranian tourist debit card through your tour operator.

faq.question: What is the dress code for women in Iran?
faq.answer: By law women must cover their hair with a headscarf and wear loose clothing that covers the arms and legs. A long tunic or manteau over trousers is standard. In practice enforcement fluctuates and dress in the big cities is fairly relaxed, but the requirement remains law for visitors too.

faq.question: Is Iran safe to visit?
faq.answer: Street crime is low and travelers consistently report warm hospitality, but many governments — including the US, UK and Canada — advise against all travel because of the risk of arbitrary detention and regional tensions. Dual nationals face particular risk. Weigh the advisories seriously and keep insurance and registration in order if you go.
